Just posted this on Reddit recently regarding crippling depression:

For me it was a combination of drug use escapism, social life upheaval, and a burgeoning awareness of the "big picture." I got a full ride to a private school 1000 miles from home, left behind all my friends and long term high school gf and sank into a terrible depression. My friends I made at school shared the common interest of getting high and that was about it. The loss of the relationship with my gf hurt way more than I was ever expecting it to.

To rationalize all these negative feelings I began to use this place to look for more and more examples of why the world was a broken place undeserving of my love. I wanted the external world to provide reasons for my internal feelings and struggle. I wanted something to blame, someone else to judge.

Dropped out of school because I only showed up regularly to one class. Dropped all contact with new friends. Returned home and isolated myself from all my old friends out of shame. Began working 55+ hours a week between 2 min. wage jobs so I wouldn't have time or energy to think about my failure.

Met back up with ex-GF in summertime. Put a lot of eggs in that basket that continuing a relationship with her would fix me. Ended up basically having a psychotic breakdown in front of her. Cut her permanently out of my life and shut myself away from everyone out of shame.

Quit both jobs no call no show. Lived on savings as a complete shut in for one month. Couldn't even bother to seek out drugs. At the end of my rope in more ways than one.

Complete psychotic break triggered by the approaching end of my apt. lease, lack of social interaction, and lack of funds or a plan for the future. Institutionalized for two weeks and pumped full of meds.

Taken in by an old ex BF of my ex GF of all people. My parents wanted nothing to do with me at this point. We hadn't hung out in high school, but he was a very caring guy that opened up his apt. to other people like myself that had nowhere else to go but the streets.

Two months of living there and another psychotic break and institutionalization for 2 weeks. Welcomed back to friend's place. Made it another month then another psychotic break and institutionalization.

During this institutionalization I finally reached a level of mental clarity that motivated me to make a change. Once released started working again. Worked and lived with friend for a year then moved out with a new coworker I had started a relationship with.

New coworker GF had worse mental health than I did. Lesson learned, we attract people that are at our same level of mental health/vices/shared activities. Within 2 weeks I had a 4th psychotic break. Nearly died, but that wasn't the goal in my mind at the time. Institutionalized for a month. Pumped full of such strong drugs I was a total zombie. Returned to old job by boss's good grace. Within 2 weeks both me and my coworker GF are fired because of my zombie like condition and my GF's alcoholism.

GF turns to stripping for income. I have enough income saved up so I pay for everything for the next 4 months. Have a 5th psychotic break because I never leave the apt.

New roommate moves in to help with burden of bills. I start to look for a job again. Get hired. Get arrested and sent to jail for charges dating back to my 4th psychotic break.

Jail was an amazing experience. No sarcasm. Much better than being institutionalized. I had a whole month of peace with no drugs that induced akathasia like I was mandated to take while in a psych ward. I ate, read, wrote, and slept for a month and regained my mental clarity. In a psych ward there is never a guarantee of discharge and you feel like you are always being judged every minute. In jail there is a legitimate process and time table. The structure relieved a lot of stress.

Got out of jail with my charges plead down to misdemeanors. Got a job within a week. Kept that job for 8 months until I got a better job and kept that one through present. Finished up my probation. Haven't touched drugs or alcohol in over 2.5 years. I'm sure medications work for some people, but they did me much more harm than good. The best medicine turned out to be sunlight, diet, and exercise. All three things I was sorely lacking in my life.

The real enemy I was battling besides depression was shame. Shame was a powerful crippling beast. I still wrestle with it to this day. The real thing that helped me flip the switch to recovery was turning inward. I stopped looking for things outside myself to blame and just focused on what I could do each day one day at a time.

Nothing hinders progress like believing the lie that you are a victim. You may have been a victim yesterday, but today is a new day and is entirely what you make of it. It is your choice to take one step away from a place you don't want to be rather than burn another day feeling sorry for yourself or your situation and stagnate. Hopelessness will eventually turn to desperation. That was the pattern of all my psychotic episodes. Long stretches of depressive hopelessness that coalesced into a backlash of manic desperation.

Since I made (slow) changes to my diet, social circles, substance usage, and exercise habits I haven't even felt depressed in over a year. I've been down a day or two or sad from external circumstances, but life hasn't felt hopeless or desperate. The shame may never fully go away, but it was also responsible for the initial kick to turn my life around.

Mental illness is very, very real. Believe me. Whether or not everyone claiming to have what could be considered a "mental illness", however, is up for debate.
